To include and organize APIRouter instances in a larger FastAPI application, you can use the `app.include_router()` method. This method allows you to add an `APIRouter` instance to your main `FastAPI` application. Here's how you can do it:

```python
from app import routers  # Assuming routers are defined in a separate module

app.include_router(routers.users.router)
app.include_router(routers.items.router)
```

This approach keeps your code organized by separating the routes for different modules (like `users` and `items`) into their own `APIRouter` instances. The `app.include_router()` method ensures that all the path operations from the included routers are included in the main application, allowing you to maintain a clean and modular structure. For example, in the `main.py` file, you would include the routers like this:

```python
from app import routers

app.include_router(routers.users.router)
app.include_router(routers.items.router)
```

This way, you can manage different parts of your application separately while keeping them integrated into the main application.
